resources.string: Not paired yet — open Pair to scan the WebUI QR.

If secret widgets show masked values, open Widgets to refresh — re-pairing rotates the encryption key, so older cached values stay hidden until the next poll fetches fresh ones. Details: docs/pairing.md in the project repo.
Allow notifications to see server alerts on this phone.
Notifications are off — new alerts won\'t show. Turn them on in Settings.

Shizuku access is powerful: granting it lets this app run anything ADB can (read logs, change settings, take screenshots, control the screen). Only enable it if you trust this device build and your backend is protected by a strong, unique password — anyone with backend access could otherwise control this phone.

Notifications use one channel per kind, plus any channel the server names explicitly — channel names match their ids so you can find them in system settings. Android keeps a channel's sound and importance once created: changing them later means adjusting that channel in Settings, or the app recreating it. Old per-kind channels from earlier builds are removed automatically; channels the server names are never deleted.

Home-screen widgets: placing one asks which row it shows — pick a cached row or leave it unassociated, and tap the widget any time to change the pick. A widget with no pick shows “Not associated — tap to choose”. If the server removes the picked row, the widget shows the same unassociated state until you pick again (the chooser names the gone row so you know what disappeared).

Secret values stay masked (“value hidden — needs refresh”) whenever they can't be decrypted, with no distinction between causes. Details: docs/pairing.md and docs/setup.md in the project repo.

This forgets the server connection and clears cached widgets on this phone. The server keeps its own device record — remove it in the WebUI if you don\'t want this phone listed. You can pair again any time with a fresh code.
